newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia govt may take YUKOS, SIDANKO shares for debt.
newsitem.headline: Russia govt may take YUKOS, SIDANKO shares for debt.

text.p: Russian oil firms SIDANKO and YUKOS may have to hand over controlling stakes in subsidiaries to the trust of the state or issue bonds to restructure debts to the state, former First Deputy Prime Minister Vladimir Potanin said on Tuesday.
Last week the government issued a regulation stating that companies with debts to the state are to transfer 50 percent plus one share in trust to the Russian Federal Property Fund.
Under the scheme companies get a five-year restructuring period on the original debt and 10-year restructuring period on fines on that debt.
If a company does not meet scheduled debt payments twice in a row or stops making current tax payments, the government has the right to sell its shares.
An indebted company may also choose to issue property-backed bonds and to restructure its original debt for two years and fines for five years.
If a company refuses to undergo any of the proposed schemes, the government will start a bankruptcy suit against it.
"I am fully convinced that if the rules of the game are set, any individual deviations from them will be most harmful," Potanin told a news conference.
A decision on each separate company will be taken by a government commission, which Potanin headed before he was dropped from the government in this week's cabinet re-shuffle.
Potanin, who used to head of one Russia's biggest banks Uneximbank before entering the govenment, will soon return to work at the bank.

The commission is due to meet next in a month to six weeks, and Potanin promised to prepare documents on unspecified companies from the SIDANKO group, the Norilsk Nickel metals giant and other firms controlled by Uneximbank.
"I think we shall be able to see results of the scheme within a month or a month and a half," Potanin said.
He also said the schemes may be applied to North-West Shipping SZRP.RTS, but it was not clear whether he intended to prepare its documents for the commission's next sitting.
Rosprom-YUKOS spokesman Vadim Razumovsky told Reuters that the suitable scheme could be chosen after the company's lawyers had studied the government's regulation.
"In any case we cannot rule out using one of the three schemes suggested by the regulation," he said.
Rosprom-YUKOS is a financial-industrial group led by Bank Menatep, which has a controlling stake in the YUKOS oil group.

Rosprom-YUKOS estimated YUKOS subsidiaries' debt to the government at 10 trillion roubles on November 1, 1996, with the debt of its main production unit Yuganskneftegaz amounting to 1.4 trillion roubles.
Previously Rosprom-YUKOS board member Sergei Generalov said that the company had managed to pay off about one trillion of the debt by February.
On March 7 the government ordered YUKOS to repay all subsidiary debts and fines.
SIDANKO, whose main production units are Chernogorneft, Condpetroleum and Varyoganneftegaz, was unavailable for comment on Tuesday.
SIDANKO's debt to the government amounted to 2.8 trillion roubles on November 1, 1996.
--Irina Demchenko, Moscow Newsroom, +7095 941 8520
